source.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
source.authors: Hoagy Cunningham; Aidan Ewart; L. Smith; R. Huben; Lee Sharkey

record.tranche_reason: The study uses activation patching with learned dictionary features to localize IOI behavior and compares feature decompositions. This is a different method from the original attention-head circuit analysis.
record.gate_note: The study tests feature-level localization of IOI in Pythia-410M, not the original GPT-2 small attention-head circuit or its head roles. Its IOI comparisons report patching efficiency against KL divergence and edit magnitude; it does not test the original circuit's faithfulness, completeness, or minimality criteria.
record.test_reason: The study uses IOI only as a benchmark for its own sparse-autoencoder features. It reports how few features (versus PCA or a non-sparse dictionary) must be patched in Pythia-410M's residual stream to move outputs toward a counterfactual. It never identifies attention heads, head classes or roles. It never compares its result with the Wang et al. circuit. It never evaluates faithfulness, completeness or minimality. So no version, including V4, is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. The authors conclude that sparse autoencoder features localize IOI counterfactual behaviour in Pythia-410M with fewer patches and smaller edits than PCA, and that a non-sparse dictionary does not show this advantage. They note that the dictionaries do not fully reconstruct activations, and that higher sparsity raises the minimum KL. They expect, but have not shown, that the result generalizes to other tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses sparse-autoencoder dictionary features and activation patching in Pythia-410M, with ACDC ordering and KL divergence from a counterfactual target; the original claim concerns an attention-head circuit in GPT-2 small.
record.method_sensitivity: At layer 11, sparse dictionary features outperform PCA in patch count and edit magnitude, but the advantage does not occur for the non-sparse dictionary (α = 0). The authors also report that larger sparsity coefficients increase minimum KL divergence because reconstruction accuracy is lower.

fits_no_version.finding: In Pythia-410M's residual stream (layer 11, 50 IOI prompts), patching a few SAE dictionary features moves outputs toward the counterfactual. This takes fewer patches and smaller edits than PCA, and the advantage disappears for a non-sparse (α=0) dictionary. Other layers appear only in a figure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI counterfactual behaviour in a mid-size LM is mediated by a small number of sparse residual-stream features, localizable more tightly than with PCA components.

record.problems: The IOI comparisons are qualitative in the extracted text and provide no numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The feature-patching analysis concerns Pythia-410M rather than GPT-2 small and does not test whether the original attention-head circuit is complete or faithful.

untested.parts: All: the 26-head GPT-2 small circuit, its 7 classes, and faithfulness, completeness and minimality.
All: backup name-mover heads under ablation.
All: no head classes or roles are identified in Pythia-410M, and component reuse is not examined.
All: the SAE or ACDC feature localization is never compared with the head circuit's components.
All: the original circuit's faithfulness or completeness is not evaluated under any ablation, metric or prompt distribution.
All: no name-order, template or multi-name variants are tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' with V4 rows is wrong. 'Method-independent' in V4 means other methods recover the same IOI circuit, and this study never relates its features to the circuit's heads. All IOI results are numberless curves in Figure 3 and Figure 17, with no uncertainty reported. The study is in a different model (Pythia-410M) from the original (GPT-2 small).

versions.untested_parts: The 26-head circuit, its seven classes and roles, and the faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
Whether backup name-mover heads take over after ablation of the main name-mover heads.
Whether the same head classes and roles carry IOI in other models, sizes, or checkpoints, or whether components are reused for other tasks.
Whether other ablation types and metrics recover the same circuit; whether the compared feature decompositions recover the same attention-head components and roles.
The original circuit's faithfulness or completeness under different ablations, metrics, or prompt distributions, and whether it explains only part of IOI behavior.
Whether the same mechanism carries IOI across name orders, templates, or sentences with more names.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The sparse dictionary reaches a given KL divergence with fewer patches and smaller edits than PCA, while the reported advantage does not occur for the non-sparse dictionary; method choice affects the reported localization efficiency (r1-r4). This comparison does not establish whether the same circuit components were recovered.
